gloss: to hum a tune; to sing to oneself

definitions.gloss: to hum a tune; to sing to oneself
definitions.explanation: To sing softly or hum a melody, typically while doing something else, often indicating a good mood.

examples.japanese: {鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}いながら{歩|ある}く。
{機嫌|きげん}がいいと{鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}う{癖|くせ}がある。
examples.english: I have a habit of humming when I'm in a good mood.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}をしながら{鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}っていた。
{彼|かれ}は{知|し}らない{曲|きょく}の{鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}っていて、{気|き}になった。
examples.english: He was humming an unfamiliar song, and it caught my attention.

notes:
{鼻歌|はなうた} (humming, nose-singing) + を + {歌|うた}う (to sing). Humming with the mouth closed or half-closed, typically while doing other activities. Often implies being in a pleasant or relaxed mood.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}いながら: while humming
- {鼻歌|はなうた}{交|ま}じりに: with a hum mixed in; humming as one goes
- {鼻歌|はなうた}が{出|で}る: a hum comes out (involuntarily, from good mood)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口|くち}ずさむ: to hum, to murmur a song — more literary; can refer to quietly singing words as well as humming
- {歌|うた}う: to sing — full singing, not just humming

USAGE:
The verb is {歌|うた}う (godan), conjugating as {歌|うた}わない, {歌|うた}って, etc. While {鼻歌|はなうた} can also be used on its own as a noun, the full expression {鼻歌|はなうた}を{歌|うた}う is the natural way to describe the action of humming.
